_comment: THE FUNDER PASS, BRIEF 12 ITEM 3. The funders' OWN publications, read against the whole
ladder population, so that rung 4 stops being a question nobody asked.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. D-L2 found rung 4 reported `not_searched` on 71 of 171 scored
entries: nobody had read a funder list for them, and recording that as the project's
failure was a claim about the project made out of a gap in this register's reading. The
brief's rule closes it: ONCE A FUNDER'S LIST HAS BEEN READ, RUNG 4 IS `searched: true`
FOR EVERY ENTRY THE LIST COVERS, AND ABSENCE FROM THE LIST IS A FAIL.
D41 IS CORRECTED, AND IT WAS WRONG ABOUT THE PUBLISHER AND NOT ABOUT THE FETCH. That
ruling recorded that 'the EU's own grant registers are unreadable to a declared reader',
measured on four presscorner and CINEA URLs that answered HTTP 200 with a 40-character
body. Re-measured on 17 September 2026, the same presscorner HTML still refuses --
ip_22_3298, ip_22_5676, ip_24_837 and the presscorner API all answer 200 with an empty
body. WHAT IS NEW IS THAT THE SAME DOCUMENTS ARE SERVED ELSEWHERE, IN FULL, BY THE SAME
PUBLISHER: the Commission's own state-aid case PDFs at ec.europa.eu/competition, the
DG COMP participant infographics, the CINEA news articles, and for some references a
presscorner print PDF at /api/files/document/print/. Eleven Commission documents
totalling 15 MB were read this way. The closed door was one route, not the register.
AN AWARD IS MATCHED BY IDENTIFIER OR BY A DOCUMENT NAMING BOTH, NEVER BY A NAME STEM.
Every match below carries `matched_on` saying which, and the sentence that does the
naming. Three near-misses are recorded as REFUSED matches with the reason, because a
name that nearly fits is exactly what the machine-classification ruling was written
about: eNRG Lahti is Nordic Ren-Gas at Lahti and this register holds Ren-Gas at Pori;
Kristinestad PtX is Koppoe Energia and this register holds Plug Power at Kristinestad;
IPCEI Hy2Use's Oersted project is Oersted Hydrogen NETHERLANDS off Zeeland and this
register holds Oersted at Idomlund in Denmark.
AWARDS TO PROJECTS OUTSIDE THE POPULATION STAY ON THE FUNDING LAYER WITH NO ROW, per
the brief. They are listed under `unmatched_awards` so the funding layer is complete
and so the next admission pass has them.
NOTHING HERE EDITS A ROW. data/transition/funding.json is untouched by this pass; what
a match produces is a rung 4 cell in the computed ladder and a queue line.
